LH-REG-002.question: An insurer incorporated in Bermuda wants to sell life insurance policies to residents of New York. Under the New York Insurance Law, this company is classified as:
LH-REG-002.explanation: Insurance Law section 107(a) defines an alien insurer as one incorporated or organized under the laws of a foreign nation. A foreign insurer is one organized under the laws of another U.S. state, which is the tempting choice but applies only to companies formed within the United States.

LH-HLTH-009.explanation: ACA major medical plans are guaranteed issue with no preexisting condition exclusions. New York goes further: Insurance Law section 3231 requires community rating, so premiums may not vary by health status, age, sex, tobacco use or occupation.

LH-HTYP-023.explanation: The federal Medigap open enrollment period lasts 6 months from age 65 and Part B enrollment, and insurers must issue any plan they sell without regard to health. New York goes further: Insurance Law section 3231 requires Medicare supplement insurers to accept applicants at any time of year at community rates.

LH-HTYP-028.explanation: LTC policies must be at least guaranteed renewable, cannot require prior hospitalization and must offer inflation protection, as New York's 11 NYCRR 52.25 requires. Partnership policies help with Medicaid rather than block it: New York Partnership plans protect assets equal to benefits paid or, under Total Asset plans, all assets.

LH-HPRV-001.explanation: Insurance Law section 3216(d)(1) requires a 10-day grace period for monthly premiums, so coverage continues through June 11 and any unpaid premium can be deducted from a claim. The 7-day period applies only to weekly premiums, and 31 days applies to other modes.
